subject: SLA baseline & remedy cap discussion — NovusCloud
messages:
From: Sierra Patel <sierra@novuscloud.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@novuscloud.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Aug 2024 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template — baseline uptime and monthly credit cap

Karthik —

Thanks for sending the initial SLA template. We reviewed internally and have two items we'd like to discuss before we move to signatures:

1) Baseline uptime: NovusCloud needs a 99.95% uptime commitment for our production region (us-east). Our concern is that some of your default templates are at 99.9 or 99.5 depending on model classes — we need confirmation you can guarantee 99.95 across the models we'll use (mixed hosted and dedicated).

2) Monthly remedy cap: we are comfortable with a cap on credits, but the proposed 25% monthly cap is too high for procurement. We'd like to target 10% cap with an initial ramp for the first three months (to cover onboarding instability) at 15%.

We attached our redlines (Novus_redlines_0819.docx) and flagged a few latency carveouts related to batched inference and scheduled model maintenance that we'd like explicitly written into the exception section. Can your team confirm whether maintenance windows and model-quantization fallbacks are treatable as maintenance carveouts or if they'd still count against the uptime metric?

Happy to hop on a quick 30-min call if that's easier.

—Sierra
Procurement Manager, NovusCloud

Attachments: Novus_redlines_0819.docx
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Sierra Patel <sierra@novuscloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@novuscloud.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Aug 2024 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template — baseline uptime and monthly credit cap

Sierra — thanks for the clear feedback and the redlines. Quick reply to the two asks and next steps: 

- Baseline uptime: we can commit to a 99.95% monthly availability for the specific model endpoints you list in the SOW, provided those endpoints are pinned to the same model variant (no automatic variant fallback). For mixed hosted/dedicated traffic we need to scope which routes are covered — I'll annotate the SOW draft.

- Monthly remedy cap: we can move on the cap but need to propose a middle ground. What we typically offer is a tiered remedy that both limits absolute exposure and preserves measurable remediation incentives. Initial proposal (see below) — open to counter: 
  * 99.95% and above: no credit
  * 99.5%–99.95%: 5% of monthly invoice
  * 99.0%–99.5%: 12% of monthly invoice
  * below 99.0%: 20% of monthly invoice
  Cap: 15% monthly (we can do 18% for first 90 days onboarding if that helps).

Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance (announced 72h) and emergency safety patches with post-facto notification are carveouts. Long-running queued maintenance for planned model conversions will be treated as scheduled provided the SOW lists the change windows. Unplanned quantization fallbacks will count toward availability unless we agree in advance and list as planned conversion.

I've attached SLA-draft-v3.pdf with inline comments and a suggested redline that implements the tiered remedy approach. If you want us to reduce the cap further we need to offset by shortening the remedy bands (i.e., smaller steps before a credit triggers).

Happy to take a call — I'm available tomorrow 10:00–12:00 PT.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA-draft-v3.pdf
From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@novuscloud.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Sierra Patel <sierra@novuscloud.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Aug 2024 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template — baseline uptime and monthly credit cap

Karthik / Sierra — quick follow up from engineering: we are okay with a tiered remedy but we have two constraints:

1) Procurement cap target: we need the steady-state monthly cap at 10% (not 15). If you must keep 15% as the operational cap, can you add a clause that limits payouts to 10% unless Novus triggers a formal remediation review?

2) Canary / rollouts: Novus requires contract language that ensures canary rollouts (for model updates) do not retroactively count as outages if they run for less than a rolling 4-hour window per change and affect <2% of production traffic. That carveout is critical for us.

If you can accept both items we can proceed to legal redlines.

—Marcus
VP Engineering, NovusCloud
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@novuscloud.com>, Sierra Patel <sierra@novuscloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Aug 2024 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template — baseline uptime and monthly credit cap

Marcus — appreciate the specifics. Proposed counter (to align commercial and engineering):

1) Monthly cap: steady-state cap of 12% monthly. We will include a governance clause: any payout above 10% requires a joint remediation review (30-day window) and sign-off from both parties' technical leads. That gives you procurement comfort while preserving operational safety.

2) Canary/rollouts carveout: we will add a carveout that excludes brief, targeted canary rollouts from uptime calculations provided the rollout meets ALL of the following:
   - Impact window per rollout <= 4 hours,
   - Affected traffic <= 2% of total production QPS,
   - Canary is documented in the change log with pre-change notification to Novus at least 24 hours prior (email to your SRE alias).

3) Onboarding uplift: We can make the first 90 days post-go-live an elevated cap period at 18% to cover shakeouts; after which the cap steps down to 12%.

If that sounds reasonable I can ask legal to produce a tight redline and we can route to DocuSign. Also looping Laura from Product/Legal to confirm carveout wording.

Best,
Karthik

Attachments: ops-exceptions-notes.txt
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@novuscloud.com>, Sierra Patel <sierra@novuscloud.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Aug 2024 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template — baseline uptime and monthly credit cap

Karthik / Novus team — internal note then public: internally, Product is comfortable with the canary carveout language above but requests we add a requirement that Novus provides a post-change traffic report for any canary that hits the 2% threshold (to avoid stealth regressions). Also, Legal will convert the governance sign-off (for payouts >10%) into a concrete acceptance checklist (roles, timeframe, and artifacts).

Public note: we accept Novus' request for a steady-state cap reduction pathway. Updated commercial summary (to reflect in the SOW):
  * Availability commitment: 99.95% monthly for scoped endpoints (listed in SOW)
  * Tiered remedy bands: 99.95%+/0% credit; 99.5%–99.95%/5%; 99.0%–99.5%/12%; <99.0%/20%
  * Monthly cap: 12% steady-state; 18% first 90 days on-boarding
  * Payout governance: payouts >10% require joint remediation review within 30 days and explicit sign-off
  * Canary carveout: as described (<=4h, <=2% traffic, 24h pre-notification) plus a post-change traffic report if canary approaches threshold.

If Novus agrees I'll ask Legal to issue a redline by end of next week and route to your procurement for signature.

—Laura Bennett
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
